note: A SECOND fixture table, minted for kogaki#625 item 1 and deliberately NOT a change to evolved.json — that table's whole claim is that a moved handoff and an added entry point run with zero driver changes, and editing it to carry a new property would make its evolvability evidence a different table's. This one carries the GATE property: a wait whose declaration the executor can actually COMPOSE, beside evolved.json's CLOSING_CONFIRMATION, whose declaration is owed-and-unwritten because this runtime binds no option composer to it. The pair is the point — the same executor must write one and refuse to invent the other.
licensed_by: v1, kogaki#625 acceptance item 1, PR #671 round 1. The `--input` refusal at a gate wait, the capture's option validation and the owed-and-unwritten refusal were all shipped asserted by nothing; this table is what a check can drive them with, seam-free.
governing_text: specs/spec-terrain/SPEC.md §15.1 — a new state is a table row PLUS a renderer, and the executor interprets the table and invents neither

state_kinds.compute: no owner surface, no renderer needed
state_kinds.wait: the executor stops; the owner speaks; re-enter with --input
state_kinds.terminal: the end of a run, read from the table and never from position

states.does: Seam-free no-op: this table exercises the GATE path and composes no material.

states.owner_supplies: up to three Strand ids, or free text
states.note: Named STRAND_SELECTION deliberately: GATE_WORK binds its option composer by STATE ID, so this is how a fixture table reaches a composer at all. The ids come from --ids, which is the composer's own declared input.

counted_baseline_note: Counted against this table's own states array, exactly as the shipped table's is. The four keys are the ones check-terrain-workflow.sh asserts present. kogaki#625: `grammared_writing_states` is declared as 0 rather than omitted. The runtime DERIVES five keys and this table declared four, so that key's comparison was disabled here and the omission passed — which is the hole PR #664 round 2 found in the shipped table's own assertion, open on the fixtures because block 2 carried no omission assertion at all. Zero is the honest figure (this table has no write state) and a declared zero is a different silence from an absent key.
